sanskrit: tasyā āhananaṃ kṛtyā menir āśasanaṃ valaga ūbadhyam asvagatā parihvṛtā | agniḥ kravyād bhūtvā brahmagavī brahmajyaṃ praviśyātti ||
english: The kṛtyā strikes her blow; the meni is her curse; the valaga is the noose; she wanders without a horse, hemmed in on all sides. Having become the flesh-devouring fire, the brahman-cow, upon entering, devours the one who has wronged a brahman.

sanskrit: sarvāsyāṅgāni mūlāni vṛścati chinatty asya pitṛbandhūn parā bhāvayati mātṛbandhūn | vivāhāṃ jñātīn sarvān api kṣāpayati brahmagavī kṣatriyasyāpunardīyamānā ||
english: She cuts and severs the roots of all his limbs; she causes his father's kinsmen to perish, and his mother's kinsmen as well. The brahman-cow, when not returned by the kṣatriya, burns away all his relatives by marriage and all his kin.

sanskrit: avāstum enam asvagam aprajasaṃ karoty aparāparaṇo bhavati kṣīyate | ya evaṃ viduṣo brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyo gām ādatte ||
english: She renders him homeless, without cattle, without progeny; he becomes unable to pass beyond and wastes away — the kṣatriya who thus takes the cow of a knowing brahman.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ vai tasyāhanane gṛdhrāḥ kurvata ailavam | (…) tasyādahanaṃ pari nṛtyanti keśinīr āghnānāḥ pāṇinorasi kurvāṇāḥ pāpam ailavam ||
english: Soon indeed at the striking of him do vultures perform the ailava rite. The dishevelled ones dance around his burning place, beating their breasts with their hands, performing the evil ailava.

sanskrit: (…) tasya vāstuṣu gaṅgaṇaṃ kurvate vṛkāḥ | kṣipraṃ vai tasya pṛcchanti yat tad āsīd idaṃ nu tāt ||
english: Wolves howl in his homesteads. Soon they ask of him: what was there once — where now is it, O father?

sanskrit: chindhy ā chindhi pra chindhy api kṣāpaya kṣāpaya | ādadānam āṅgirasi brahmajyam upa dāsaya ||
english: Cut, cut through, cut to pieces; burn down, burn utterly away. O Āṅgirasī, make subservient the brahman-wronger who seizes.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevī hy ucyase kṛtyā kūlbajām āvṛtā oṣantī samoṣantī brahmaṇo vajraḥ ||
english: For you are called the Vaiśvadevī, the kṛtyā enveloped in kūlbajā plants, burning and consuming utterly — the thunderbolt of the brahman.

sanskrit: kṣurapavir mṛtyur bhūtvāpidhāvitaḥ | ā datse jinatāṃ varca iṣṭaṃ pūrtaṃ cāśiṣaḥ ||
english: Having become Death with a razor's edge, she pursues him. She takes away the radiance of those who conquer, along with the fruit of oblations and charitable gifts and their blessings.

sanskrit: ādāya jītaṃ jītāya loke 'muṣmin pra yacchasi | aghnye padavīr bhava brāhmaṇasyābhiśastyā ||
english: Having taken what is won, you hand it over to the victorious in that other world. O Aghniyā, follow the path; be the curse of the brahman-wronger.

sanskrit: meniḥ śaravyā bhavāghād aghaviṣā bhava | agnhye pra śiro jahi brahmajyasya kṛtāgasaḥ ||
english: Become the meni, become the arrow; become the deadly poison of evil. O Aghniyā, smite off the head of the brahman-wronger who has committed transgression.

sanskrit: tvayā pravṛktaṃ rajatam agnir dahatu duṣkṛtaṃ devapīyum arādhasam | vṛśca pra vṛśca chindhi pra chindhi kṛnta pra kṛnta piṃśa pra piṃśauṣa sam oṣa daha pra daha | brahmajyaṃ devy aghnya ā mūlād anu saṃdaha ||
english: Let fire burn the silver set in motion by you, the evil deed of the god-scorner and the ungrateful one. Hack, hack through; cut, cut apart; slash, slash to pieces; tear, tear asunder; scorch, scorch completely; burn, burn utterly. O goddess Aghniyā, burn the brahman-wronger from the root throughout.

sanskrit: yat te śīrṣaṇi daurbhāgyaṃ saktaṃ keśeṣu nihitaṃ lalāṭe | ayaṃ tad viśvabheṣajo apāmārgo 'pa lumpatu ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is clinging to your head, lodged in your hair, placed upon your forehead — let this Apāmārga, the universal healer, wipe that away.

sanskrit: yat te bhruvor daurbhāgyaṃ karṇayor akṣṇor hitam | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is seated in your eyebrows, placed in your ears and eyes — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: (yat) te mukhe nāsikāyāṃ daurbhāgyaṃ vācy oṣṭhayoḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is in your face and nostrils, in your speech and lips — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te datsu daurbhāgyaṃ jihvāyāṃ chubuke hitam | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is placed in your teeth, in your tongue, in your chin — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: (yat) te manasi saṃkalpe daurbhāgyaṃ prāṇa āhitam | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is deposited in your mind and intention, in your vital breath — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te hanvor daurbhāgyaṃ kaṇṭhe klomasu viṣṭhitam | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is spread through your jaws, in your throat and lungs — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te skandheṣu grīvāsu daurbhāgyaṃ kīkasāsv anūkye | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is in your shoulders and neck, in your vertebrae and spine — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te doṣṇor daurbhāgyam aṃsayor upapakṣayoḥ | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is in your forearms, in your shoulders and armpits — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te bāhvor daurbhāgyam aratnyoḥ kalkuṣīr anu | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is in your upper arms, along your elbows and wrists — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].

sanskrit: yat te hastayor daurbhāgyaṃ pāṇyor aṅgulīr anu | (…) ||
english: Whatever ill-fortune is in your hands, along your palms and fingers — [let Apāmārga wipe that away].
